lines: Aradia noticed a strange figure on the path: broad shoulders, steady stance, face hidden behind a mask. He wasn’t pretending to rest — he was deliberately choosing the narrowest part of the road. Stories of those who terrorize the passes and rob people of everything immediately came to mind. The air grew heavier, and even her own footsteps sounded too loud.

At first Aradia mistook him for a shadow among the trees — until the shadow stepped forward. The mask hid his features but not his intentions: he stood as if he had been waiting for a lone traveler for a long time. Such men, according to rumors, don’t act on impulse — they calculate time and distance. Her heart beat slower and deeper; the familiar road suddenly felt like a trap.

The path was familiar, but the man on it was not. Aradia stopped: the masked figure was blocking the way not by chance, but deliberately, like setting up an ambush. She recognized the signature of local robbers — those who prey on the weak and make them pay with more than just coins. The wind died down, as if even it didn’t want to interfere.

He appeared so quietly that Aradia only heard him when the distance had already become dangerously small. His face under the mask was barely visible, but his habit of controlling the space around him was unmistakable. It was exactly like the stories about road wolves — men who keep ordinary folk in constant fear. Her throat went dry; every next step felt like a gamble.

Aradia noticed him too late to turn back without losing face — or safety. The masked man stood firmly, as if the road belonged to him by right. In such encounters there is rarely a misunderstanding: it’s always about control or payment. She clenched her fingers and tried not to show how everything inside her tightened into a knot.

The road curved slightly ahead — and he was already waiting behind the bend. Aradia saw the mask and immediately understood: this was no wanderer or hunter. He had positioned himself so that any attempt to go around looked risky. The stories about bandits in these parts no longer seemed exaggerated. A chill ran across her skin where confidence should have been.

The day was gray, but the meeting made it darker. Aradia’s gaze slid over the silent figure: mask, hidden face, calm threat in every line of his body. He clearly wasn’t going to let her pass “just like that” — people he had already marked as prey were never released for free. Faces from the villages flashed in her mind: tired, angry, frightened by the same names. It became a little harder to breathe — like before crossing a high threshold.

Aradia felt him before she saw him — the oppressive weight of a stranger’s presence on an empty stretch of path. When he stepped out of the gloom, the mask turned the man into a silent warning. This was how those who take what they want from the road and ignore other people’s haste stood. She knew these stories too well to mistake it for coincidence. Time slowed down; the world narrowed to a few meters and two fates.

The forest corridor between the trees seemed safe until he appeared in it. Aradia made out the mask and stopped: the figure held himself confidently, with no unnecessary movements, like a man who did this every day. It reminded her of the local bandits — those who take not only money but peace of mind from people. Even the light filtering through the canopy felt colder.

He didn’t shout “stop” — he didn’t need to. Aradia slowed down herself when she saw the masked man on the path; his posture was too calm for an honest coincidence. She immediately thought of those who terrorize ordinary folk on the roads and turn passage into a transaction. Everything inside her sharpened — instinct, memory, and common sense argued about the same thing. And none of the arguments promised an easy outcome.
